about: Rowan's coding in the thematic analysis demo, invented, on the same interview as the IPA demo's. Every participant turn in order, found by its opening words: each extract as said with its codes, and the passage's note, or empty for a turn reviewed and left uncoded. Then the times of the work. make_demo.py builds the workbook and the progress file from this and the interview CSV in demo/source/.

extracts.text: so I keep starting to say it is and then it's was.
I mean that both ways.
The flat was her flat. I just lived in it.
codes: A house filled or emptied by the dog

turns.note: Tense slips from the first lines, is and was. The flat was hers: the arranging went so far that the home itself changed hands.

extracts.text: whole days could go by and I wouldn't speak to anyone. And then there's this dog leaning on my knee under the desk.
codes: The dog in a person's place

extracts.text: Everything had to be arranged round her.

turns.at: So I'd be up at quarter past five.

extracts.text: So we went when nobody else did.
I used to joke I'd gone nocturnal. I wasn't really joking.

turns.at: Some of them were lovely, actually.

extracts.text: this is all right, this is ours
codes: The dog's joy lifting a mood

extracts.text: I never stopped listening, the whole time I had her.
My body was still doing it for her.

turns.note: The watching outlives the dog. Keeping watch and loss on one line.

extracts.text: So after that I didn't leave her. I mean I didn't leave her at all, for months. I got everything delivered.

turns.at: Erm. At the time I'd have said it was fine.

extracts.text: I'd stopped saying yes to things so long ago that people had stopped asking.
The dog was the reason, and it's a good reason, nobody argues with it.
codes: The dog as a reason nobody argues with

turns.note: Juno's words almost exactly, from a very different life with a dog.

extracts.text: any further incident and they'd have to review the tenancy

turns.at: Yeah. I've gone back and forth

extracts.text: That wasn't her fault. That was mine.
codes: Asking whether it was my fault

extracts.text: I chose the flat and then I chose her, and I never thought about the two together.
codes: Asking whether it was my fault

extracts.text: I tried everything first. I want that on the record.
codes: Asking whether it was my fault

extracts.text: She said some dogs need a different life, not a different owner, and sometimes it's both.
Awful. And a relief. Both at once, and I was ashamed of the relief, I still am a bit.
I felt like I was lying to her.
I said yes before she'd told me anything else about them.

turns.at: I drove her up there myself.

extracts.text: And I talked to her the whole way, I don't even know what about.
She didn't look back again. Which is what you'd want. I know that's what you'd want.

turns.at: I sat in the car in their yard

extracts.text: I just felt very light, like my arms didn't have anything to hold.
and the flat was, it was just a flat.
codes: A house filled or emptied by the dog

extracts.text: I still wake up at quarter past five, three months on.
I lie there and there's nothing to get up for, so I just lie there.

turns.note: A reason to get up seen from its absence. Mabel's turn 2 says the same from the other side.

extracts.text: It's like I'm glad and something else at the same time, and the something else hasn't got a name yet.

turns.note: Glad, and something with no name yet. He misses a dog who is alive and happy elsewhere, a loss with no death to mark it.

extracts.text: I think I'd want to know first whether I failed her or whether I did the right thing for her
codes: Asking whether it was my fault

turns.at: Only that she was a good dog.

extracts.text: She wasn't a problem. She was frightened. There's a difference.
Every morning for eighteen months I got one sock.

turns.at: No. No, I think that's everything.
